corpus.title: Serbia’s Vucic Calls Early Parliamentary Elections for October 25
corpus.signal_text:
Serbia’s Vucic Calls Early Parliamentary Elections for October 25
Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic on Tuesday set a date for early parliamentary elections on October 25, signing a decree dissolving parliament and the decision calling the elections – in which he is expected to run for prime minister, facing down a strong challenge from opponents.
“We need election results that will clearly demonstrate and determine the will of the citizens as to where, in what direction, and along which path Serbia is heading,” he said, adding that Serbia has been enduring “turbulence for more than a year and a half”.
Student-led protests have gripped the country since November 2024, sparked by the collapse of a railway station canopy in Novi Sad that left 16 people dead, sparking nationwide outrage over alleged official corruption and negligence. The protests have posed the strongest challenge to Vucic’s Serbian Progressive Party since it came to power in 2012.
Vucic claimed the “turbulence” in society was not merely the result of “conflicts between political parties or political actors here in Serbia” but also involved “significant interference by foreign powers”. He and his Progressive Party have often claimed that foreign states, including European countries, have been involved in supporting or inciting the student-led protests.
In his comments on Tuesday, however, he also insisted that Serbia, an EU candidate state, had chosen “a good European path, while [also] preserving traditional friendships, national pride, and dignity” – referencing Belgrade’s continued friendly relationship with Russia.
As one of the reasons for calling early elections, Vucic cited the organisation of the high-profile international EXPO 2027 exhibition, which will be held in Belgrade starting in May next year.
“If it were not for these tensions, if it were not for these political disagreements and conflicts, we certainly would not need [elections]. But any delay would jeopardise both EXPO and the survival of democracy as the best form of political system in our country,” he said.
On Monday, Prime Minister Djuro Macut proposed the dissolution of parliament, which was adopted by the government and sent to the President as part of the official procedure.

corpus.signal_text:
Александр Вучич объявил дату внеочередных выборов в Сербии
Президент Сербии Александр Вучич распустил 9 сентября парламент страны и объявил, что внеочередные выборы пройдут 25 октября. Тем самым президент выполнил главное требование сербских студентов, которые протестуют уже почти два года и чей «Студенческий список» станет главным оппонентом властей на предстоящих выборах. Последние опросы дают преимущество правящей партии, и ее победа позволит Александру Вучичу пересесть из президентского кресла в премьерское, оставаясь у руля, по крайней мере, еще четыре года.
«В последние полтора с лишним года Сербия прошла через период потрясений, вызванный не только конфликтом партий внутри страны. При значительном вмешательстве внешних сил мы получили беспорядки, конфликты и в итоге — разделенное общество. Если бы не эти напряженность, разногласия и конфликты, досрочные выборы были бы не нужны. В то же время их откладывание ставит под угрозу проведение в нашей стране Всемирной выставки ЭКСПО-2027» — так президент Александр Вучич, обращаясь в полдень 9 сентября к нации, объяснил необходимость проведения 25 октября досрочных выборов.

Serbia's President Vucic dissolves parliament, calls snap elections

BELGRADE, Sept 9 - Serbia's President Aleksandar Vucic on Wednesday dissolved parliament and announced snap elections for next month as he seeks to extend his hold on power by running for prime minister.

corpus.title: Vucic dissolves Serbian parliament; early elections set for October 25
corpus.signal_text:
BELGRADE, September 9. /TASS/. Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has approved the decision to dissolve the current National Assembly (unicameral parliament) and call early elections for October 25.
"Acting on the government's proposal, I am issuing a decree to dissolve the National Assembly. The decree enters into force on the day of its publication. I am announcing elections for members of parliament and scheduling them for October 25," Vucic said in an address to the nation.
On September 7, Prime Minister Duro Macut submitted a proposal to Vucic to dissolve parliament - a necessary step for holding snap elections. Prior to this, Milos Vucevic, leader of the ruling Serbian Progressive Party, announced that Vucic would lead the party's ticket in the upcoming parliamentary elections and serve as its candidate for prime minister.
